questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Botswana?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Botswana on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Botswana article.

questions.proof: The countries that border Botswana are Zimbabwe, South Africa, and Namibia.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Gaborone?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Botswana is Gaborone.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Botswana on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Botswana on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Botswana?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Botswana article.

questions.proof: The capital of Botswana is Gaborone.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Botswana about 581,737 square kilometres; Zimbabwe about 390,757 square kilometres; Eswatini about 17,364 square kilometres; Seychelles about 459 square kilometres.
